2.1.2.heading: Quiet reset alerts
2.1.2.alerts: Reset alerts fire once per real reset again, instead of every second while Claude Code is open.

2.1.1.heading: Sign in and weekly limits fixed
2.1.1.signin: Google, GitHub and email sign in finish in the app again, and a refused sign in names its error code.
2.1.1.weekly: When an older terminal runtime is installed, the Usage tab shows the one command that updates it, so weekly limits stay visible.
2.1.1.commands: Every command the app shows is pinned to this version, stuck background refreshes no longer pile up on Windows, and DeepSeek shows its official mark.

2.1.0.heading: One number per bar
2.1.0.claude: Claude now shows one number per bar, with the Claude bucket allowlist, clear status line captions and the Pro captions preset. Setup upgrades the runtime when needed.
2.1.0.desktop: The desktop opens faster and its buttons work. Connect repairs a Codex connection that stopped reading. Usage, Connect Tools and Settings share a responsive window.
2.1.0.phone: The phone app can install to the Home Screen, follow its light or dark theme, keep the last bars when offline and show the Pro tab.
2.1.0.status: The terminal line uses short captions such as 5h, 7d, fable7d, cx7d and ag5h. Money cells such as or $ keep their amounts, and an OpenRouter management key adds your balance.

2.0.4.heading: More accurate limits
2.0.4.codex: Codex limits now use OpenAI's documented source. Your Codex sign in stays on your device.
2.0.4.claude: Claude now shows Current session, Weekly, all models, Weekly, Fable and extra usage. Fable and extra usage are on after one notice, with switches in Settings and the terminal.
2.0.4.providers: Antigravity can refresh from its CLI. OpenRouter, Grok, Moonshot, Kimi, OpenCode and Gemini now label their limits more clearly.
2.0.4.sync: Unreadable readings never sync, and stale bars are flat grey.

2.0.3.heading: One screen, every tool
2.0.3.screen: Every tool and API key now fits on one screen.
2.0.3.tools: Claude Code stays visible while idle. Antigravity shows again with a clear open button.
2.0.3.money: Each API key shows its own amount. DeepSeek is included, and the terminal can show all six money cells.
2.0.3.pro: Sign in works again, and Pro now unlocks trials, period end days, comps, devices and reconnects.
2.0.3.setup: Terminal setup recovers after host edits. Phone setup includes install help and code entry.

2.0.2.heading: One small tab, a clearer Home
2.0.2.edge: One small tab on the left edge of your screen replaces the Rail. Hover it to see your limits and agents. On Linux Wayland the tray takes its place.
2.0.2.home: Home shows the account you are signed in with now, one card per tool. Anything that cannot be measured waits on Connections with one fix.
2.0.2.statusline: The terminal status line leaves out the folder and any provider that cannot be measured right now.

2.0.1.heading: Startup fix
2.0.1.startup: Fixes a freeze at startup on Windows.

2.0.0.heading: Your limits and agents, in view
2.0.0.rail: The left edge Rail keeps your readings in view on Windows. The macOS and Linux Rail is a preview; the tray remains available.
2.0.0.activity: See when a supported agent is busy, waiting for you, or done. Local activity and usage alerts are free.
2.0.0.statusline: The terminal status line uses the same band colours as your meters. Toggles let you choose which providers appear.
2.0.0.cursor: Cursor is Experimental. Live account verification is still required, and a missing quota stays unavailable.
2.0.0.retry: The desktop and CLI share one retry policy. Refresh respects provider retry deadlines and keeps the last reading with its original time.
2.0.0.sessions: Phone and browser sessions handle renewal, pairing and reconnects more reliably. Older readings remain clearly marked when a computer stops syncing.
2.0.0.spend: The local monthly spend cap is removed. Local spend readings remain free, with one active account per provider.
